maturity_definitions.PROVEN: Implemented and exercised by a relevant committed automated or integration test across the stated capability boundary; this does not imply production certification.
maturity_definitions.IMPLEMENTED_BUT_UNPROVEN: Executable implementation exists, but the repository does not contain a test that proves the stated boundary or real external-system behavior.
maturity_definitions.PARTIAL: A useful subset exists, but material advertised inputs, semantics, or end-to-end links are absent or incomplete.
maturity_definitions.STUBBED: The surface exists primarily as static/demo behavior or a placeholder without the advertised backend capability.
maturity_definitions.DORMANT: Implemented code/data contracts exist but are intentionally outside the active V1 product path.
maturity_definitions.DUPLICATED: Two or more active implementations represent substantially overlapping concepts without one unambiguous canonical owner.
maturity_definitions.DEAD: No reachable runtime, API, CLI, frontend, or test path was found and the code has no documented active role.
maturity_definitions.MISSING: No implementation of the stated capability was found.

capabilities.name: FastAPI backend process
capabilities.notes: Registers 127 /api/v1 operations plus /health; startup creates SQLAlchemy tables.

capabilities.name: Topo Agent long-running discovery process
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Plugin collection, heartbeat, buffering, checkpoint and failure-signal submission are exercised with fakes; real infrastructure access is connector-specific and not proven.

capabilities.name: Kubernetes discovery
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Core workload, service, ingress and EndpointSlice inventory exists; Kubernetes client behavior is mocked in tests and supported resource coverage is bounded.

capabilities.name: AWS inventory discovery
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Multiple AWS resources and relationships are implemented, but tests prove only selected enrichment and cache behavior, not live AWS collection.

capabilities.name: Azure inventory discovery
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Broad Resource Graph normalization exists; no live subscription integration test is committed.

capabilities.name: GCP inventory discovery
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Compute, GKE, hierarchy and asset inventory exist; no live project integration test is committed.

capabilities.name: Host, process, Docker and socket inventory
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Executable collectors and graph enrichment exist without focused end-to-end tests.

capabilities.name: Tetragon/eBPF runtime ingestion
dependencies: external source SDK or local runtime API
capabilities.notes: Parser, aggregation, sensor heartbeat and deployment artifacts exist; live Tetragon-to-backend behavior is unproven.

capabilities.name: Immutable topology snapshots
capabilities.notes: Manual and automatic snapshots are persisted as serialized GraphSnapshot payloads; immutability is enforced by service convention rather than database constraints.

capabilities.name: Continuous topology checkpointing
capabilities.notes: Meaningful-change triggers, digest dedupe, debounce metadata, periodic reconciliation and incident-boundary behavior are covered.

capabilities.name: Logical identity resolution
capabilities.notes: Deterministic rules and overrides exist, but graph entity ID constructors remain inconsistent across some ingestion paths.

capabilities.name: Source-to-runtime chain
capabilities.notes: Repository, commit, workflow, image and workload links exist in subsets; no single committed test proves the complete chain and Helm is absent.

capabilities.name: Topology snapshot diff / normalized change intelligence
capabilities.notes: Snapshot differences produce durable normalized changes and meaningful topology changes can promote durable change events.

capabilities.name: Native change-event model and correlation
capabilities.notes: Durable events and links exist; provider-resource-to-graph identity matching is not uniformly canonical.

capabilities.name: Native change-source webhooks
capabilities.notes: GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Azure DevOps and Terraform Cloud contracts exist; only selected normalization/security cases are tested.

capabilities.name: Internal failure-signal to incident lifecycle
capabilities.notes: Deterministic qualifying failures, correlation, safe pinning, entity resolution, pending reconciliation, durable RCA and briefing handoff are covered by an integration-style repository test.

capabilities.name: Legacy signal orchestration and incident analysis
capabilities.notes: Active advanced workflow persists IncidentAnalysis separately from canonical IncidentRecord and Block 13C CausalAnalysis.

capabilities.name: Evidence-backed causal RCA (13C)
capabilities.notes: Deterministic ranking and evidence graph are tested; confidence is a heuristic composite score, not a calibrated probability.

capabilities.name: Blast-radius traversal
capabilities.notes: Pinned-snapshot bounded-depth traversal exists, but there is no focused blast-radius test file and traversal treats all relationships as undirected.

capabilities.name: Ownership and business impact (14A)
capabilities.notes: Resolution, aggregation and operational context are exercised; ownership mappings are current-state, not temporally versioned.

capabilities.name: Response plan (14B)
capabilities.notes: Read-only investigation/mitigation guidance and validation checks are deterministic and tested.

capabilities.name: Resolution and outcome intelligence (14C)
capabilities.notes: Responder evidence, action attribution and timing are durable and tested with conservative ambiguity handling.

capabilities.name: Historical incident similarity (14D)
capabilities.notes: Explicit weighted deterministic similarity with bounded history and optional annotation-only AI.

capabilities.name: Historical response intelligence (14E)
capabilities.notes: Historical support can annotate but cannot create current actions; raw counts and conflicts are preserved.

capabilities.name: Execution readiness (14F)
capabilities.notes: Thoroughly tested read-only safety contract, intentionally excluded from the V1 briefing and cockpit.

capabilities.name: Human approval control plane (14G)
capabilities.notes: Durable approval state/audit exists but is not needed by V1 incident intelligence.

capabilities.name: Execution transaction foundation (14H)
capabilities.notes: Intent and internal claim primitives exist; no public claim/execute endpoint, worker, or infrastructure executor exists.

capabilities.name: Unified incident briefing (15A)
capabilities.notes: Orchestrates existing RCA, context, plan, history and outcome services with optional annotation-only AI.

capabilities.name: Incident cockpit and incident home
capabilities.notes: Live briefing contract, lifecycle pending state, progressive disclosure and no execution controls are tested.

capabilities.name: Ask Topo frontend
capabilities.notes: Static demo content; it does not call a backend question-answering contract.

capabilities.name: CLI simulator frontend
capabilities.notes: Browser simulator is static and distinct from the real Python CLI.

capabilities.name: Python operational CLI
capabilities.notes: Broad API coverage exists, but tests focus mainly on Blocks 14A-15A and dormant execution contracts rather than every command.

capabilities.name: API token authentication
capabilities.notes: Bearer token and agent-specific auth exist; API authentication is disabled by default and general routes lack fine-grained authorization/tenancy.

capabilities.name: Outbound webhook notifications
capabilities.notes: Configuration, dispatch and delivery audit exist without focused delivery integration tests; secrets/headers are stored in application records.

capabilities.name: Central OpenAI annotation client
capabilities.notes: Responses API, store=false, redaction and deterministic no-key/provider-failure fallback are tested.

capabilities.name: LLM provider unification
capabilities.notes: Four active legacy services call Groq directly in addition to the centralized LLM client.

capabilities.name: Database migrations and production schema lifecycle
capabilities.notes: No Alembic/migration directory exists; startup uses Base.metadata.create_all.

capabilities.name: Tenant isolation and broad RBAC
capabilities.notes: Principal roles exist for approval/execution policy only; topology, incident and connector records have no tenant boundary.

capabilities.name: Prometheus/Alertmanager, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic and ITSM connectors
capabilities.notes: The normalized failure-signal contract is an extension point, but vendor adapters are not present.

capabilities.name: Autonomous remediation/execution
capabilities.notes: No executor or Kubernetes/Terraform/cloud mutation path exists; this matches the read-only V1 boundary.
